_comments: THE RENEWAL PASS (issue #243). `AutoRenew` and `RenewalLeadDays` have had a consumer for some time,
and that consumer has never been called: `Orders.SpawnRenewals` is a remote operation, and no
browser opens itself the week a customer's term expires. This row is the caller.
IT SHIPS DISABLED, AND IT SHIPS SET TO PREVIEW, and both are deliberate rather than cautious
duplication. They guard different mistakes:
· `Status: Disabled` keeps a lower environment from quietly scheduling live billing the moment
this metadata lands in it.
· `Preview: true` means that even an enabled job writes nothing — it reports the list and stops.
Going live is therefore two named acts, not one, and the second one is the act that starts billing
customers. That is the go-live gate the issue is asking for an owner and a date on.
THE ORDER OF THE TWO: enable first, read the run's Candidates output, confirm the list, THEN set
Preview to false. Enabling a preview job is reversible; the first live pass is not, because a
placed renewal order is a confirmed order with a ledger entry behind it.
03:00 UTC, AFTER ACCOUNTING'S 02:00 ERP MASTER DATA SYNC. A renewal order resolves GL accounts as
it books, so it should run on the day's master data rather than yesterday's. The hour is otherwise
unremarkable: the operation is date-based, not time-based, and a run at any hour of the right day
selects the same subscriptions.
DAILY, THOUGH THE LEAD WINDOW IS MEASURED IN MONTHS. The window is 90 days wide for most types, so
a subscription entering it is due for many consecutive days and a missed day costs nothing. Daily
is for the OTHER direction: it keeps any single pass small, so a configuration mistake surfaces as
a handful of wrong orders rather than a quarter's worth.
· ConcurrencyMode `Skip` — the operation's guards make a double-run a no-op, but two passes
racing on the same subscription would both read 'not yet renewed' before either wrote.
· MissedRunPolicy `RunOnce` — a week of missed days is one catch-up, not seven. Seven passes
would select the same set seven times and the guards would reject six of them; running the
same work six times to be told no is not a catch-up.
· RunImmediatelyIfNeverRun `false` — a first deployment must not bill anybody before somebody
has looked at the list.
· MaxRuntimeMinutes 30 — the operation is LongRunning and each renewal is a full booking
transaction, so the lease has to outlast a batch rather than a single write.
`MaxCount` IS THE FIRST-RUN SAFETY VALVE, not a throughput setting. It caps what one pass can place,
so a mis-set lead day invoices 25 customers and gets noticed rather than invoicing the book. The
remainder is not dropped — those subscriptions are still due tomorrow. Raise or remove it once a
few live passes have been read.
· The cap binds on a PREVIEW identically, which is what makes the gate meaningful: the
Candidates list a person confirms is the same 25 the pass places once Preview goes false,
rather than every subscription in the 90-day window.
OwnerUserID / NotifyUserID are deliberately unset: they name people, which differs per environment,
and a metadata row that asserted one would overwrite whoever the host had chosen.

fields.Name: Orders — Spawn Renewals (daily)
fields.Description: Places renewal orders for subscriptions whose latest term expires inside their own lead window and whose holder consented via AutoRenew. Ships disabled and set to Preview: enable it, confirm the Candidates list on the run, then set Preview to false to begin billing.
